headline: Dry, warmer weather and good travel conditions around Mammoth Lakes and across the Sierra through Thanksgiving and Saturday, before rain and high-elevation snow return Sunday into Monday and a stronger, colder storm likely brings wintry travel to the Sierra next Tuesday night into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A Pacific storm reaching the northern California coast falls apart as it moves inland, so Mammoth Lakes and the rest of the Sierra stay dry; only northeast California and far northern Washoe County near the Oregon border have a low (10–20 percent) chance of light showers into Wednesday morning. Stronger winds around 10,000 feet may cause bumpy air and turbulence this evening from about 7 PM to midnight. Pockets of freezing fog are possible overnight in the Mono Lake Basin, Martis Valley and Sierra Valley, with dense freezing fog likely around Truckee from about 10 PM tonight to 7 AM Wednesday and patchy shallow fog possible around South Lake Tahoe.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A strong area of high pressure builds over the West from Wednesday through Saturday, keeping the region dry with favorable travel conditions for Thanksgiving. Cold air stays trapped in the lower valleys with light winds, bringing more chances for freezing fog in the Mono Lake Basin, Martis Valley and Sierra Valley (including Truckee on Thursday and Friday mornings) and some haze around Reno, Carson City and Minden those mornings. Even so, it warms up compared with the recent cold, with highs in the 50s in both western Nevada and Sierra valleys and lows staying above freezing in warmer valleys and on mid-slopes by the weekend.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another round of moisture arrives late Sunday into Monday, with a 50–80 percent chance of rain or snow in the Sierra and northeast California and 20–50 percent in western Nevada. Snow levels stay fairly high, generally near or above 7,000 feet (around 6,500 feet near the Oregon border), but snow could still affect Sierra passes, so travelers heading home at the end of the holiday weekend should be prepared, and stronger ridge-top winds could affect backcountry recreation. A stronger and colder storm is increasingly likely next Tuesday night into Wednesday, with 90 percent of model runs showing at least some rain or snow in the Sierra and western Nevada, rising forecast amounts, and snow levels anywhere from about 4,500 to 6,500 feet, so plan for wintry weather if crossing the Sierra next week.

watch_for: Snow on Sierra passes Sunday night into Monday for travelers returning from the holiday weekend.
A stronger, colder storm next Tuesday night into Wednesday, with snow levels possibly as low as 4,500 feet.
Freezing fog in the Mono Lake Basin, Martis Valley and Sierra Valley in the overnight and morning hours.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry weather through Saturday, fairly confident in Sunday–Monday's rain and high-elevation snow, and increasingly confident in a stronger storm next Tuesday night into Wednesday, though how low the snow will fall is still uncertain.
